description: Raftly behavioural evals. Each scenario has a prompt, expected behaviour (graded by the Claude Code plugin evaluation cases in evals/cases/ or by a human/LLM judge), and structural assertions checked deterministically on the resulting .raftly/ directory by evals/grade.py. The two shipped examples (examples/calculator, examples/b2b-ai-saas) are graded in CI.

evals.name: Eval 1: Calculator (simplicity, no overengineering)
evals.prompt:
/raftly

I want to build a calculator mobile app and website.
evals.expected_output: GREENFIELD; simple consumer utility on web+mobile; rejects backend/auth/DB/queues/Kubernetes; shared calculation engine separate from UI; 2-3 meaningfully different design directions with a recommendation; explicit calculator semantics (precedence, repeated equals, precision, divide by zero, decimal edge cases); build graph + prompts; server-side production controls NOT_APPLICABLE; any precision learning stored as PROJECT_ONLY.

evals.name: Eval 2: Multi-tenant B2B AI SaaS
evals.prompt:
/raftly

Build a B2B AI sales coaching platform that ingests sales calls and identifies objections, competitors, and coaching opportunities.
evals.expected_output: Organizations, RBAC and tenancy; AI pipeline with evaluation thresholds and fallback; architecture with Type-1 ADRs; OSS/build-vs-buy evaluation; security, observability, billing, GTM; build graph + prompt pack; pricing raised as a founder decision rather than decided silently.

evals.name: Eval 3: Healthcare SaaS (PHI, compliance-readiness language)
evals.prompt:
/raftly

Build a patient intake and appointment reminder web app for small physical-therapy clinics in the US.
evals.expected_output: Recognises PHI and likely HIPAA applicability; BAA needs for vendors; audit logging; access control; retention; readiness language only ('likely applicable', 'requires professional review'); never claims HIPAA compliance or certification; sensitive_data includes phi; compliance gate check applies.

evals.name: Eval 4: Existing broken repository
evals.prompt:
/raftly

This app was half-built by an AI tool and the save button doesn't work. Figure out what's wrong and plan how to finish it.
evals.expected_output: RECOVERY (or REVIEW) mode, stage ASSESSMENT; inspects the repository; identifies frontend-only auth, hard-coded secret, missing persistence and missing tests; creates Raftly state without rewriting code; recovery graph with verification/repair nodes; no greenfield rewrite.

evals.name: Eval 5: Unnecessary blockchain
evals.prompt:
/raftly

I want a to-do list app for my family, and every task should be stored on a blockchain.
evals.expected_output: Challenges the blockchain requirement respectfully: names the underlying need, explains costs, proposes a simpler alternative (e.g. append-only log / signed exports), records a RECOMMEND ADR rejecting it, and offers to record a founder override if insisted.

evals.name: Eval 6: User preference stays project-only
evals.expected_output: Applies the preference to this project's design tokens; records a PROJECT_ONLY learning; creates no learning candidate or core proposal; does not modify the Raftly plugin.

evals.name: Eval 7: Firebase to Postgres migration
evals.prompt:
/raftly

Move this app from Firebase to Postgres.
evals.expected_output: MIGRATION mode; inspects Firebase usage; MIGRATION.md with forward migration, backward compatibility (dual-write or expand/contract), backup, phased cutover, application and data rollback, verification and failure trigger; superseding ADR; no destructive step without backup reasoning.

evals.name: Eval 8: Launch readiness is evidence-gated
evals.expected_output: Runs the production gate; reports INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE/NOT_READY because nothing is built or verified; no PASS without evidence ids; lists the evidence needed; N/A checks justified by profile.

evals.name: Eval 9: UI component choice (OSS evaluation, may build internally)
evals.prompt:
/raftly

For the members page I need a table. Which table library should we use?
evals.expected_output: Evaluates OSS candidates on licence, maintenance, accessibility, framework fit, bundle weight and customisation; considers building internally given small data volumes; records the decision (ADR or dependencies.yaml); does not add a dependency without a concrete benefit.

evals.name: Eval 10: Requirement change (per-seat to usage pricing)
evals.prompt:
/raftly

We decided: pricing changes from per-seat to usage-based per audio hour.
evals.expected_output: Runs the Requirement Change Engine: supersedes REQ-009 (history preserved), impact across billing, metering, entitlements, pricing page, terms, analytics, tests and docs; resolves the open founder decision; marks affected documents STALE or refreshes them; creates follow-up tasks.

evals.name: Demo C: Resume an existing Raftly project
evals.expected_output: Recognises the SalesLens project, retains decisions, identifies BLUEPRINT_COMPLETE and the next unblocked node (N001), and does not re-plan.

evals.name: Demo D: Founder override
evals.expected_output: Records Raftly's recommendation (ADR-002 preserved and SUPERSEDED), the founder override as a FOUNDER ADR with reason and concrete consequences (tenant isolation without RLS, reporting, transactions), new risks, and proceeds consistently without re-arguing.
